title: Per-site settings in a child frame must key to the top page origin and read it exclusively — location.href inside an iframe is the embed domain, and OR-ing both levels lets stale entries override the toggle forever
trigger: A per-site/per-URL toggle (tokenize, enabled flags) is read inside a cross-origin iframe — the user toggles on the top page but the iframe keeps the old state, or auto-enables regardless of the toggle
principle: Two failure layers: (1) location.href in a child frame is the embed domain (playembed.vip), not the page the user sees — resolve the top origin via location.ancestorOrigins[last] or document.referrer; (2) an OR gate over key levels (frameUrl || topOrigin) resurrects stale entries at any level — the embed domain entry can pin the feature on after the user turns it off. Child frames: read the top origin's flag exclusively (origin-level, not page-level keys — other top pages' subtitleUrls entries also leak through an isEnabled(topOrigin) URL check); fall back to frameUrl only when the top origin is unresolvable.

cases.context: Onflix embeds playembed.vip; tokenize toggle writes subtitleOrigins['onflix.lat']. An older build had written subtitleOrigins['playembed.vip']=true + subtitleUrls['playembed.vip/player']=true. User toggles OFF → onflix.lat=false, but the OR gate over frameUrl keeps enabled=true forever — 'auto tokenize, ignores my toggle'.
cases.bad: enabled = isEnabled(ts, location.href) || isEnabled(ts, topOrigin)  // stale playembed:true wins
cases.good: enabled = topOrigin !== undefined ? ts.subtitleOrigins[topOrigin] ?? false : isEnabled(ts, location.href)

applyFor: any per-site flag read inside embed iframes (tokenize, subtitles, features)
multi-level settings keys where a lower-priority level can hold stale data
child-frame code that needs the embedding page's identity — ancestorOrigins/referrer suffice, no postMessage needed
